SOURCE 1 (RBC GAM Executive Summary, December 2025, https://www.rbcgam.com/en/ca/article/executive-summary-new-year-2026/detail) forecasts 'moderate economic growth' and SOURCE 7 (CIBC Asset Management, December 2025, https://www.cibc.com/en/asset-management/insights/fixed-income/fixed-income-investing-as-rates-fall.html) states 'In the U.S., growth is expected to slow, and inflation is projected to remain above target before gradually easing.' However, SOURCE 5 (Scotiabank, December 10, 2025, https://www.scotiabank.com/ca/en/about/economics/economics-publications/post.other-publications.economic-indicators.scotia-flash.-december-10--2025--1.html) indicates Chair Powell wanted to 'turn this job over to whomever takes over with the economy in really good shape,' suggesting growth remained resilient. The exact 2% figure is not confirmed in the sources, making this a directional rather than precise hit.

overall_analysis: Vanguard's prediction captured the broad dynamics of 2025 but with mixed precision. The institution correctly identified that supply-side drivers (particularly AI) would continue while policy risks posed headwinds, and accurately anticipated growth deceleration. However, the specific tariff impacts and the precise 2% growth target were not fully validated by year-end outcomes, which showed more resilience and selective tariff effects than the prediction suggested.

statements.reasoning: The reality context contradicts this prediction. SOURCE 1 (RBC GAM, December 2025, https://www.rbcgam.com/en/ca/article/executive-summary-new-year-2026/detail) confirms 'stocks will continue to outperform bonds' and 'inflation subsiding sufficiently to motivate continued interest-rate cuts,' indicating the classic soft-landing outcome did occur. SOURCE 5 (Scotiabank, December 2025, https://www.scotiabank.com/ca/en/about/economics/economics-publications/post.other-publications.economic-indicators.scotia-flash.-december-10--2025--1.html) confirms 175bps of rate cuts, supporting lower bond yields. The soft landing with higher stock prices and lower yields materialized contrary to the prediction.
